stem: In a toddler with suspected bronchiolitis or viral wheeze, which statement best describes the role of a nasopharyngeal aspirate (NPA)?

options.text: It is the key investigation because it directly changes management
It should always be done before supportive care starts
It may support bronchiolitis diagnosis if RSV is positive, but it does not change management
It is mainly used to decide whether salbutamol can be tried in infants under 1 year
It is only useful after 7 to 8 years of age

explanation: NPA may support the diagnosis of bronchiolitis if RSV is detected, but it does not change management, which remains supportive.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: 3.2 Chronic Airway Problems

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because NPA is not the key test for directing treatment in bronchiolitis or viral wheeze.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because supportive care does not depend on doing an NPA first.
optionExplanations.C: Correct because a positive RSV result can support the diagnosis of bronchiolitis, but the result does not alter management.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because NPA is not used to decide whether salbutamol can be trialled.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because there is no age-related role like this for NPA in this setting.

sourceRefs: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
